title: The CPU and the fetch-decode-execute cycle
explanation: The CPU fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, then executes it, repeating continuously. Von Neumann architecture stores both data and instructions in the same memory.

title: CPU performance
explanation: Performance depends on clock speed (instructions per second), the number of cores (parallel processing), and cache size (fast memory close to the CPU that reduces trips to slower RAM).

title: Primary storage: RAM and ROM
explanation: RAM is volatile (fast, but cleared when powered off) and holds currently running programs and data. ROM is non-volatile and holds instructions needed to start the computer, such as the BIOS.

title: Secondary storage and units
explanation: Secondary storage (SSD, HDD, optical) keeps data permanently. Units scale as: bit, byte (8 bits), kilobyte, megabyte, gigabyte, terabyte, each roughly 1000x the last.

title: Converting between number bases
explanation: Computers store data in binary. Hexadecimal is a shorthand for binary that's easier for humans to read, since each hex digit represents exactly 4 bits.
code:
value = 200
print(format(value, "08b"))  # binary: 11001000
print(hex(value))            # hex: 0xc8
print(int("11001000", 2))    # back to denary: 200

title: LANs and WANs
explanation: A LAN covers a small, local area (like a school building), typically owned by one organisation. A WAN spans a larger geographical area and often uses infrastructure owned by third parties, e.g. the internet.

title: Network protocols
explanation: Protocols are agreed rules for communication. Common examples: TCP/IP (breaks data into packets and routes them), HTTP/HTTPS (web pages), FTP (file transfer), and email protocols like SMTP and IMAP.

title: Threats to networks
explanation: Common threats include malware, phishing, brute-force attacks (trying many passwords), denial-of-service attacks (overwhelming a service with traffic), and SQL injection (inserting malicious code via an input field).

title: Identifying and preventing vulnerabilities
explanation: Defences include penetration testing (deliberately probing for weaknesses), firewalls (filtering network traffic), anti-malware software, user access levels, and keeping software patched and up to date.

title: Operating systems
explanation: The operating system manages hardware resources on behalf of applications: memory management, process scheduling (deciding what runs when), peripheral management (via device drivers), and providing the user interface.

title: Utility software
explanation: Utility software performs maintenance tasks that keep a system running well, e.g. anti-virus scanners, disk defragmentation, file compression, and backup tools.

section: 1.6 Ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impacts
title: Ethical, legal, cultural and environmental impacts of computing
explanation: Technology raises issues around privacy and surveillance, digital exclusion, environmental cost of manufacturing/e-waste, and laws such as the Computer Misuse Act (illegal access/modification of data) and the Data Protection Act/UK GDPR (how personal data must be handled).

title: Representing algorithms with flowcharts and pseudocode
explanation: Flowcharts use standard shapes (ovals for start/end, rectangles for processes, diamonds for decisions) to show the logic of an algorithm visually. Pseudocode expresses the same logic as structured, language-independent text.

title: Searching algorithms
explanation: Linear search checks every item in order until it finds a match — works on any list but is slow. Binary search repeatedly halves a SORTED list to find the target much faster.

title: Sorting algorithms
explanation: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order items until the list is sorted — simple but slow (O(n squared)). Merge sort splits the list into halves recursively then merges them back in order — much faster (O(n log n)).

title: Sequence, selection, iteration
explanation: Every program is built from three constructs: sequence (steps in order), selection (if/elif/else branching), and iteration (for/while loops that repeat steps).

title: Data types and data structures
explanation: Basic data types: integer, real/float, character, string, Boolean. A 1D array (list) stores an ordered sequence of values; a 2D array stores a grid, accessed with two indices.

title: String handling operations
explanation: Common string operations include finding length, converting case, slicing substrings, concatenating, and converting between strings and numbers.
code:
word = "OmniShell"
print(len(word))
print(word.lower())
print(word[0:4])
print(str(42) + " students")

title: Defensive design
explanation: Defensive design anticipates misuse: validating input (checking type, range, format), authenticating users, and handling errors gracefully so the program doesn't crash on unexpected input.

title: Testing
explanation: Testing checks a program works correctly using normal data (typical valid input), boundary data (values right at the edge of what's accepted), and erroneous data (invalid input that should be rejected safely).

title: Logic gates and truth tables
explanation: AND is true only if both inputs are true. OR is true if at least one input is true. NOT inverts a single input. These combine to build up the decision logic used inside a CPU.

title: High-level and low-level languages
explanation: High-level languages (like Python) read closer to English and are easier to write and maintain, but need a translator. Low-level languages (like assembly or machine code) map closely to the hardware and run faster but are harder to write.

title: Translators: compilers and interpreters
explanation: A compiler translates the entire program into machine code before it runs, producing a standalone executable. An interpreter translates and runs the program line by line, which is slower but easier to debug interactively.

title: Integrated Development Environments (IDEs)
explanation: An IDE bundles the tools developers need in one place: a code editor, a translator (compiler/interpreter), and a debugger for stepping through code and inspecting variable values while it runs.
